security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU helper_wfi(), if the U-mode WFI trap condition depends on mstatus.TW when S-mode (RVS) is implemented — i.e., a control flow where TW=0 short-circuits the illegal-instruction exception before reaching the (rvs && prv_u) unconditional trap — WFI would incorrectly execute without trapping in U-mode despite S-mode being present, violating the spec's mandate that U-mode WFI must always trap regardless of TW.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: MSTATUS_TW check in WFI handler that gates or precedes the unconditional U-mode+S-mode trap; specifically any code path where get_field(env->mstatus, MSTATUS_TW) appearing without an additional (prv_u && riscv_has_ext(env, RVS)) conjunct results in WFI completing in U-mode when S-mode exists and TW=0
security_spec.summary: WFI in U-mode with S-mode implemented must unconditionally raise illegal-instruction exception regardless of mstatus.TW; TW must only gate trapping for S-mode and for U-mode when S-mode is NOT present

findings.finding: The WFI handler correctly implements the spec requirement that U-mode WFI always traps when S-mode is implemented, regardless of mstatus.TW. The TW-dependent U-mode check at line 548 is gated by (!rvs && prv_u), ensuring it only applies when S-mode is absent. When S-mode is present (rvs=true), the unconditional (rvs && prv_u && !env->virt_enabled) check in the second disjunct catches U-mode WFI and raises an illegal-instruction exception independently of TW.

spec_citations.excerpt: When S-mode is implemented, then executing WFI in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception, regardless of the value of the TW bit, unless the instruction completes within an implementation-specific, bounded time limit.
